taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO and Flora of North America.
look_here_first: Look at the flower first: broad flat pale-green lobes are strongly netted with dark green lines, and the center has conspicuous silvery reflective anther appendages—the 'pearl.'

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — UT PRC Purola Preserve records the species among naturally occurring, non-introduced plants. Travis — UT PRC Travis County herbarium includes multiple Matelea reticulata specimens. Williamson — UT PRC Vascular Plants of Williamson County provides a detailed county treatment.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: No county inferred from statewide or ecoregion range. Legacy names are counted only where taxonomic concept is reconciled.

best_field_traits: opposite deeply cordate leaves; stems and petioles conspicuously hairy
rotate broad corolla lobes strongly dark-reticulate and glabrous adaxially
corona reduced to a very low yellow undulate ring
8–15 cm fusiform follicle, sparsely to moderately muricate
morphology_keys.milkweed_vine_training: Use fused corolla plus corona/gynostegium and follicle armature; preserve modern genus placement even when older/source labels use Matelea.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Matelea edwardsensis: M. reticulata is flatter and strongly net-reticulated, glabrous inside, denser-haired, with a highly reduced corona and silvery center; M. edwardsensis is more campanulate with mostly longitudinal lines, hairy inside, and obvious fleshy corona segments. Gonolobus suberosus var. granulatus: Anglepod has larger uniformly olive-green non-reticulate flowers and a smooth sharply angled fruit; pearl milkvine has netted flowers and a muricate follicle.
